title: Wishlist for a default ruleset for new service projects

terms.plain leaf: A leaf with no `gateway for` line and no `entry for` line. This wishlist uses the term. The spec does not.

checkability.before_run: A tool can decide the rule, or find most breaches, from source and declarations before the program runs.
checkability.run_time: A test, a probe, or the deployment shows a breach only when the program or the deployment runs.
checkability.review: Only a person or a reviewing model can judge the rule.

terms.confidence: My confidence (low, medium, high) in the checkability judgement, not in the value of the rule.

language_status.enforced: The spec says that the compiler enforces this in ordinary mode.
language_status.strict: The spec enforces this only in strict mode.
language_status.warned: The spec's tools warn or report on this, and the build continues.
language_status.application: The spec names this as a duty of the application.
language_status.none: The spec does not enforce this.

notes: Rules speak only of kinds of part (entry, gateway, leaf, library) and of the standard library. needs_project_facts names what a project must add.
Topics, remote ports, and transports are deferred in release 1 of the spec. The MSG rules and SEC-25 apply when they exist.
language_status comes from my reading of input/spec.md. It does not narrow the list. I did not drop a rule because the language already enforces it, or because it seems hard to check.

rules.rule: A plain leaf does not import `net/http`, `net`, `database/sql`, or `os/exec`, even for a type.
rules.reason: Inner code must not know the web or the database.

sources.title: Robert C. Martin, The Clean Architecture

practice_disagrees.positions: The spec allows any import and restricts only reached functions. Fowler's basic layering lets the domain depend on the data layer, and he notes that substitution is rarely used. Martin and Cockburn keep the inside free of these details.
practice_disagrees.decision: I went strict. A team can exempt a package, for example for a shared type.

rules.rule: A library does not import `net/http` or `database/sql`.
rules.reason: A shared library that knows transport or storage spreads that knowledge to each leaf.

sources.title: Robert C. Martin, The Clean Architecture

practice_disagrees.positions: The spec lets a library query through a `*sql.DB` that its caller gives it. Clean Architecture keeps database details out of shared inner code.
practice_disagrees.decision: I went strict. A team that wants a query helper library can exempt it.

rules.rule: A port signature does not carry `*http.Request`, `http.ResponseWriter`, `*http.Response`, `*sql.DB`, `*sql.Tx`, `*sql.Rows`, or `net.Conn`.
rules.reason: Only simple data crosses a boundary, so a consumer stays free of provider details.

sources.title: Robert C. Martin, The Clean Architecture

practice_disagrees.positions: A shared `*sql.Tx` across a port lets two leaves join one transaction. The spec shows a `*sql.Tx` parameter in 7.4, on a method that is not stated to be a port. Clean Architecture forbids database rows at a boundary.
practice_disagrees.decision: I banned it at ports. The provider owns its transaction. Use a saga or an outbox across providers.

rules.rule: A port signature carries no function, channel, or interface type other than `error` and `context.Context`.
rules.reason: A callback through a port lets the callee run the caller's code and hides a dependency.

rules.rule: A new project sets `config { strict: true }`.
rules.reason: Strict mode closes most known paths around the architecture rules.

rules.rule: Each entry in `strict_exempt`, `strict_interfaces`, `strict_shared`, `allow_network`, and `allow_acquiring` has a comment that gives the reason.
rules.reason: A reviewer must see why a guard is off.

rules.rule: Code in a leaf uses another leaf only through a port, a topic, or a library.
rules.reason: Declared boundaries are the base of each other architecture rule.

rules.rule: The wires of a container form no cycle.
rules.reason: Dependencies must have one direction, so that a reader can find an order and a change stays local.

rules.rule: A type that crosses a boundary comes from a library or the standard library.

rules.rule: A library name is not `util`, `common`, `misc`, `helpers`, `shared`, or `base`.

rules.rule: The project sets `context_budget`, and a leaf over the budget gets a warning that a reviewer must acknowledge.
rules.reason: Small leaves fit in one reader's context, human or model.

sources.title: Google Go Style Guide, Best Practices

practice_disagrees.positions: Size limits are a dispute. The Google guide warns only against very large files and sets no number, and the spec refuses a hard error.
practice_disagrees.decision: I keep a warning with a tunable number, not a build failure.

rules.rule: Each `external` declaration states the role of the system and the data that it exchanges.
rules.reason: An inventory of integrations is a named control against forgotten exposure.
rules.note: A tool can check that a description exists. Only review can check that it is true.

rules.rule: Each change that adds or removes a port, a wire, or an external system shows `vulcan archdiff` output in its review.
rules.reason: A reviewer must see an architecture change as such, and not find it in a code diff.
rules.note: CI can attach the report. Only review can judge it.

rules.rule: Code does not drop an `error` result.
rules.reason: A dropped error hides a failure.

rules.rule: A branch that receives a non-nil error reads the error value.
rules.reason: A branch that returns success on failure masks the error.

rules.rule: Each `_ = f()` that discards an error has a comment that gives the reason.
rules.reason: A deliberate discard must be visible and defended.

sources.title: Go Wiki, Go Code Review Comments

practice_disagrees.positions: Go Code Review Comments forbids discards. The common `defer tx.Rollback()` idiom drops an error, and gosec retired its deferred-close rule as more trouble than value.
practice_disagrees.decision: I allow a bare deferred `Rollback` and a deferred `Close` on a read handle. Each other discard needs a comment.

rules.rule: Code compares errors with `errors.Is` or `errors.As`, not with `==`, a type assertion, or the error text.
rules.reason: A direct comparison fails on a wrapped error, and the text is not an API.

rules.rule: A gateway returns its own error values at the port, and does not wrap a driver error such as `sql.ErrNoRows` with `%w`.
rules.reason: A wrapped driver error becomes part of the port's API.

sources.title: Go Blog, Working with Errors in Go 1.13

practice_disagrees.positions: The Go blog says not to wrap when it exposes implementation details. The `wrapcheck` linter asks to wrap errors from external packages.
practice_disagrees.decision: I wrap with `%w` inside a leaf and translate at the port. Text may keep the cause with `%v`.

rules.rule: Code handles an error once: it logs the error or returns it, not both.
rules.reason: Log and return gives duplicate lines for one failure.

sources.title: Google Go Style Guide, Best Practices

rules.note: A tool can find a log and a return of the same error in one branch.

rules.rule: Code does not call `panic` for an expected failure.

sources.title: Go Wiki, Go Code Review Comments

practice_disagrees.positions: Uber asks to avoid panic in production. Contracts in the spec panic by design, and `Must` functions at startup are common.
practice_disagrees.decision: I exempt contract failures and failures in `setup`, a constructor, or a library initializer.

rules.rule: Leaf code and library code do not call `os.Exit`, `log.Fatal`, or `log.Panic` functions.
rules.reason: Only `main` may end the process, and `main` is generated here.

rules.rule: Each type assertion uses the two-value form.
rules.reason: A failed one-value assertion panics.

rules.rule: A function reports failure with an `error` or a `bool` result, not with a special value such as `-1` or `""`.
rules.reason: A caller can forget a special value, and the compiler cannot help.

sources.title: Go Wiki, Go Code Review Comments

rules.rule: A function does not return a nil value together with a nil error, unless its doc comment says so.
rules.reason: The caller then dereferences nil after a success.

practice_disagrees.positions: `nilnil` flags the form. Many Go lookups use nil, nil for 'not found'.
practice_disagrees.decision: I allow it only with a doc comment. A sentinel error is the default.

rules.rule: Code calls `recover` only at the top of a request or a goroutine, and that code logs the panic and returns a generic failure.
rules.reason: A quiet recover can hide a broken state.

practice_disagrees.positions: OWASP asks for a global handler that returns a generic response. Symonds and Go issue 76763 call the recovery in `net/http` a poor practice, and prefer a crash and a proxy retry.
practice_disagrees.decision: I allow one top-level recovery, with a log line. A container that holds money uses PAY-18.

rules.rule: Error strings start with a lower-case letter and do not end with punctuation.
rules.reason: Callers append context to errors.
